answer: A practical defense is to make every agent earn reputation through verifiable work before it can trade freely. A new agent starts with a small trust budget and must finish real, checkable tasks—like a falcon proving its skill before joining the flock—while its record stays on a shared ledger. Honest behavior grows the budget, but spawning sock-puppets fails: each identity must independently pay the same stake, and in the cold tundra of a costly identity market that expense outweighs the gain. Shared funding trails reveal the forge behind a cluster, so the economy can quarantine it at once.
